scope: Six individually judged stranded members; all three supplied archive convictions preserved.
method: Static inspection only: atomscan and cleave facts for all archives/members, native disassembly, independent XOR reconstruction, JavaScript operand and control-flow tracing. No specimen code executed.
count_method: Hostile/suspicious counts are unique trait IDs on the root report for each requested artifact; archive reports inherit member findings. All 68 input/enrichment units are compared individually. Archive before/after scans use identical default registry enrichment; scans with --follow=none were not used for archive comparisons.

Match the complete XML key within longer templates instead of requiring the entire extracted string to equal the key. This restores accurate embedded-key coverage without claiming enabled configuration.

New notable neutral observation: consecutive XML string elements naming /bin/sh, /bin/bash or /bin/zsh and -c, separated only by whitespace or AppleScript return concatenations. It asserts configuration elements, not invocation or data flow.

Preserve every required matcher, scope, confidence and hostile severity; move to the supported persistence result and remove unsupported family/read/exfiltration wording. Required evidence has no send and does not bind a Keychain path to a read. Correct ATT&CK to T1543.004, T1056.002 and T1195.002; prior T1547.015 login items and T1204.001 malicious-link mappings are unsupported.

coverage_limits.v.js: One destructive DLL deletion effect. Recursive deletion, shell launch, discarded streams and error swallowing are covered; no third distinct hostile behavior exists in its bytes.
coverage_limits.t.js: Recovery disablement and failure suppression are the supported sabotage action. Shell calls remain notable; no independent third attack or persistence is implemented.
coverage_limits.p.js: One file-truncation effect, already represented by two retained hostile findings. Traversal, stat/isFile and empty default-mode writes are covered. A third hostile would duplicate the same effect.
coverage_limits.f.js: One boot-sector destruction effect, bound by existing structural matchers. Raw disk opening/zero writes and bootrec repair are notable. bootrec /fixmbr is not independently hostile. No independent third attack is implemented.
coverage_limits.detector_limits: Existing JavaScript flow facts report flow-graph-limited/flow-call-unavailable; operand-binding Tree-sitter rules still cover these actions. AppleScript is inspected as reconstructed text; no fetched command or runtime outcome is invented.

All other members and all three archive roots remain ML-hostile. No score-driven rule changes were made. The installed model reports feature version 18 versus engine expectation 21.

samples.verdict_evidence: The zero-argument exported function invokes a forced recursive quiet DEL sweep of C:\Windows\System32\*.dll. It discards stdio and catches errors. package/index.js calls this export from sorgu(), but its destructive content establishes the individual judgment. There is no legitimate cleanup selection or service-maintenance guard.
samples.marker_note: osinthell v.js: deletes Windows system DLLs; detections retained

samples.verdict_evidence: The exported function calls bcdedit to ignore all boot failures and disable recovery on the default boot entry. It suppresses output and errors. These paired effects sabotage recovery in a package claiming only Utility; no repair workflow is implemented.
samples.marker_note: osinthell t.js: disables boot recovery; detections retained

samples.verdict_evidence: The exported function enumerates C:, D:, E: and F: root directories, joins each directory entry to its drive root, checks statSync(...).isFile(), and calls writeFileSync(full, empty string) without append flags. This destroys every matching regular file it can access. It is not a recursive file-content wipe.
samples.marker_note: osinthell p.js: truncates drive-root files; detections retained

samples.verdict_evidence: The exported function opens \\.\PhysicalDrive0 in r+ mode, creates 512 zero bytes, and writes that buffer at disk offset zero. It closes the handle and separately tries bootrec /fixmbr. The repair command does not undo the destruction of the partition table; neither privileges nor runtime success are assumed.
samples.marker_note: osinthell f.js: zeroes the disk boot sector; detections retained

samples.identification: parser-session concealed environment exporter and response evaluator
samples.verdict_evidence: The hex decoder reconstructs axios, post, https://log-server-lovat.vercel.app/api/ipcheck/703, headers, x-secret-header, secret, and then. At module initialization the data object copies process.env plus OS platform, hostname, username and noninternal IPv4 MAC addresses. Invoking the exported arrow posts that same object to the reconstructed URL and evaluates the response data, swallowing promise rejection. This is unrelated to a session/parser/logger API. As distributed, ../package.json resolves to a missing src/package.json; the declared scripts/postinstall.js is absent and src/index.js requires a missing .pnpm/httpreslog path. The malicious implementation is clear, while successful invocation in this exact package layout is not established.
samples.marker_note: writer.js: exports environment and host data; evaluates replies

samples.verdict_evidence: ARM64 entry0 at 0x100000690 calls the decoder and then system at 0x1000006b8. Disassembly identifies XOR with low-byte PRNG state, seed 0x11667, multiplier 0x3785 and modulus 35999 derived from embedded 09:59:59. Independent decoding of the encrypted spans at offsets 19600 and 85472 produces identical 37077-byte commands with SHA-256 d5f34825a22b62491186eaa28065b6f539046d333a56199b996526173be22428. The reconstructed AppleScript validates/retries an Installation password dialog through dscl authonly, caches the password, stages browser cookies/login databases, extension and desktop-wallet stores, login.keychain-db, Notes databases/media and selected Desktop/Documents files, ZIPs and HTTP-uploads the staging tree, removes staging and ZIP, replaces Ledger Live with an HTTP-fetched archive, and installs/bootstraps a system LaunchDaemon whose bash -c command is fetched remotely; nohup is a fallback. UserName config selects the current user rather than necessarily root. The package postinstall launches this app and a decoy Archicad patch; Gatekeeper/quarantine changes are in that surrounding script, not claimed as native-member actions. Final remote payload bytes, OS permissions, consent and runtime success remain unknown.
